issues.description: The problem specification and UML require a method named checkOrderReady() on SealSaloon to process and serve orders, but the solution implements this behavior in a method named processOrders() instead of providing checkOrderReady(). This name/signature mismatch between the specification and the reference implementation can confuse students (they may implement checkOrderReady while the solution uses a different name) and may cause tests or grader expectations that reference checkOrderReady() to fail or be unclear.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the reference implementation match the specification by renaming processOrders() to checkOrderReady(), or add a public checkOrderReady() method that delegates to processOrders(). Alternatively, update the problem statement and tests to use processOrders() consistently. Ensure method name and signature are identical across spec, template, and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires a SealSaloon method named checkOrderReady() (UML and textual description). The reference solution implements the same functionality using a method named processOrders(), and orderMeal calls processOrders() instead of checkOrderReady(). This creates a naming mismatch between the specified API in the problem statement and the solution implementation and may confuse students who are instructed to implement/check for checkOrderReady().
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady(), and have orderMeal() call checkOrderReady(). Alternatively, add a public checkOrderReady() wrapper that delegates to processOrders(), so the method name in the solution matches the problem specification.
